task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: causal effect of own lineup on shot selection
confounding by opponent lineup and game situation
statistical power for detecting small shot-mix differences
measurement reliability of derived play-type and shot-distance categories
multiplicity across many shot types and lineup combinations
regression to the mean when substitutions are triggered by poor performance

historical_evidence.finding: When the opposing rim big is off the floor, offenses slightly increase drives (+0.82 pp, t=3.3) and post-ups (+0.43 pp, t=2.4) and decrease three-point attempts (-1.79 pp, t=-5.8), but rim-share change is not significant (+0.12 pp, t=0.4) and overall PPP change is tiny (+0.008, t=1.1). With 1.07 M possessions the signal is described as WEAK/SMALL and insufficient to carry a paper.

A play-type forecasting model using Structural Influence after a hub sits showed no improvement over conventional features (LL gap +0.00002, Holm p=0.87). The null was adequately powered, indicating that lineup-driven play-type prediction may be very subtle even with sophisticated features.

Comparison of deterministic vs. agent-based play-type recommendation agents yielded only 40 test pairs with 8 overrides; precision was 7.5% and no player-level overrides were scorable, making the question unanswerable with that data.

Offenses do not consistently tilt play-type mix toward an opponent's prior defensive weakness; tilt -2.353 pp per PPP (t=-1.94) with a very small SD of weakness (0.017 PPP). Measurement reliability of play-type shares and game-plan adaptation was a limiting factor.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a clear own-shot-mix adaptation to opponent's lack of a rim big
failed_approaches.why: Effect sizes were small despite 1M possessions; rim-share change not significant and overall PPP null. Labelled WEAK/SMALL.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting play-type changes after a hub substitution using structural influence features
failed_approaches.why: Null result with adequate power, suggesting lineup-induced play-type shifts may be too noisy or confounded to detect with rich models.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Showing that teams adapt play mix to opponent's prior defensive weakness
failed_approaches.why: Effect in wrong direction and measurement reliability of play-type shares too low (SD of weakness 0.017 PPP).

evidence_establishes: Opponent lineup changes (e.g., rim big off) can produce measurable shifts in some shot-type frequencies (3PA, drives) even though overall efficiency may not change ([prior work]).
Large sample sizes (~1M possessions) are available with NBA play-by-play data for studying shot-mix changes.
Play-type-based analyses can suffer from low measurement reliability and small effect sizes, leading to null or inconclusive results ([prior work], SF-[prior work], [prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changes in one's own offensive five produce larger or easier-to-detect shot-mix shifts than the opponent's lineup.
Whether a within-game design that compares possessions immediately before and after a substitution can cleanly isolate personnel effects.
The specific power and minimum detectable effect size for own-lineup changes using the available three-season dataset.
That the proposed design is immune to regression-to-the-mean or confounding from simultaneous opponent substitutions.
own_inferences: Own-lineup changes are likely to have a larger influence on shot mix than opponent-lineup changes because they directly alter the shooting tendencies of the players on the floor.
A within-game, fixed-effects design that holds opponent lineup constant and controls for period, clock, and score can provide a credible causal estimate.

The detection goal is methodological ('showing the design can detect personnel effects'), so even a small but statistically significant shift in a composite shot-type distribution would satisfy the aim, provided all confounding is addressed.
A pre-registered composite test (e.g., chi-squared or multinomial likelihood ratio) will avoid multiplicity problems while answering the core question.
uncertainties: The magnitude of the shot-mix shift caused by a typical offensive substitution is unknown; prior studies only examined opponent-driven changes.
The frequency of 'clean' substitution windows where the opponent's lineup remains unchanged may be limited, reducing effective sample size.
Play-type classification from [source] database (derived from play-by-play) has not been validated for this specific task and could introduce label noise.
Whether regression to the mean due to non-random substitution timing can be fully addressed by within-game controls.

historical_effect.explanation: Without historical evidence, one might assume that any lineup change produces large shot-mix shifts that are trivially detectable. The results from [prior work] show that even a clear defensive constraint (no rim big) yields only modest, partially null effects. This shifts the design toward a more rigorous causal framework, a composite significance test, and explicit power planning to avoid the weak/small failure seen in [prior work]. It also highlights multiplicity ([prior work], SF-[prior work]) and measurement reliability (SF-[prior work]) as risks that must be mitigated.

prior_work.summary: Prior work shows that opponent lineup changes produce detectable but small shot-mix shifts ([prior work]) and that play-type-based predictions often yield nulls ([prior work], SF-[prior work]). No prior study directly tests whether own-lineup changes cause measurable shot-mix differences, but these findings indicate that power, confounding, and measurement reliability must be carefully handled.

risks.text: Even with three full seasons, some shot-type categories may have low frequency, and effect sizes may be small (as in [prior work]). A composite test will mitigate this, but power should be calculated beforehand.
Substitutions often co-occur for both teams and are correlated with game situation (score, period, rest). Failure to control for opponent lineup, game clock, and score could bias estimates.
If many individual shot types or lineup combinations are tested separately, multiplicity will inflate false positives. A pre-registered global test addresses this.
Coaches may insert or remove players after extreme events (e.g., a bad stretch), causing regression toward the mean that could be mistaken for a lineup effect.
The derived play-type categories (e.g., 'drive', 'post-up', 'spot-up') may be mis-labelled, especially if based on heuristics. Prior studies flagged low measurement reliability as a limiting factor.
Lineup membership must be determined only from information available at the time of the possession; using future rotation data would induce lookahead bias.
Rare shot types (e.g., alley-oops, post-ups) will have very low per-possession rates, making their estimated changes noisy and unreliable.

design.estimand: The average effect of a change in the offensive five (substitution) on the multinomial distribution of shot types (e.g., rim, short mid-range, long mid-range, non-corner 3, corner 3) or play types (e.g., isolation, pick-and-roll, off-screen, transition, post-up), measured per possession.
design.sample: All regular-season and playoff possessions from the 2022-23 through 2024-25 NBA seasons, excluding garbage time (defined as Q4 with >20-point differential and <5:00 remaining), end-of-quarter heaves, and possessions where the offensive or defensive lineup is ambiguous due to simultaneous substitutions.
design.power: Power analysis will be conducted using the outcome standard errors observed in [prior work] for comparable shot-type proportions. With ~1M possessions per season and a focus on a composite multinomial test, the study will have >80% power to detect a shift of 0.5 percentage points in any single shot-type category (e.g., 3PA share) at alpha=0.05, assuming baseline rates of 25-40%. If preliminary power analysis shows insufficient sensitivity, the analysis will be restricted to high-frequency categories (rim, mid-range, 3pt) and the largest plausible substitution types (e.g., centre-for-centre vs. centre-for-guard swaps).
design.controls: Within-game and within-period fixed effects; indicator variables for 2-minute clock bins; score differential (lead/trail); opponent lineup characteristics (number of traditional bigs, number of guards); and indicator for whether the substitution was a timeout or end-of-quarter break. To address RTM, we will also include a control for the previous possession's outcome (points, shot type) and test for pre-trends.
design.falsification: 1) Placebo test: Compare shot-mix changes in possessions immediately before the substitution (when the lineup is still the original one) to those after, expecting no difference if the substitution timing is unrelated to shot selection. 2) Close-match test: Among substitutions where the incoming and outgoing players share the same position and archetype (based on external clustering), the composite shift should be insignificantly different from zero. 3) Negative control: Repeat the analysis on a random, independent sample of non-substitution possession pairs to confirm that the detected shift is not an artefact of the differencing method.
design.multiplicity: A single composite hypothesis will be pre-registered: the multinomial distribution of shot types differs between possessions with the old and new offensive five. This will be tested via a likelihood-ratio test or chi-squared statistic. No separate per-category hypothesis tests will be used for the primary conclusion.
design.decision_rule: The design is declared to detect personnel effects if the composite test yields p < 0.05 (two-sided) and all three falsification criteria are satisfied (placebo test non-significant at p > 0.10, close-match test non-significant, negative control non-significant). If the composite test is non-significant, the design is considered unable to detect personnel effects with the current sample.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 play-by-play and derived play-type possessions as of 2026-11-02.
